text.p: PanAmSat Corp said on Friday the launch of its PAS-6 Atlantic Ocean Region satellite has been rescheduled until March or April 1997 because Space Systems/Loral, which is building the satellite, needed to replace the spacecraft's power control units.

PanAmSat, which provides global satellite services, said it expected minimal impact on its business because of the delay. PanAmSat said it planned to use the satellite for direct-to-home satellite services into Latin America.
The satellite was originally set to be launched by Arianespace in December 1996, the company said.
PanAmSat said Arianespace indicated it could accommodate the revised timetable.
The company also said it expected future PanAmSat satellite launches to proceed on schedule.
"PanAmSat fully supports every effort by Space Systems/Loral to deliver spacecraft that have improved reliability," said Frederick A. Landman, PanAmSat's president and chief executive officer.
Space Systems/Loral decided to replace the power control units with an improved design.
